reason: Mechanism is real: binding.go:186-198 matches on the address alone, so a reader bound at the same address replaces the URL binding and URL.Query loses taint (reproduced woven via the fallback handler plus the net/url advice). Triggering it requires a hand-built *http.Request whose Body type embeds url.URL at offset 0 with req.URL pointing to it. Server paths (HTTP/1, HTTP/2, h2c) always use separate allocations, and the real-server control keeps taint. The effect is a false negative only. Only a code comment (binding.go:93-94) records the one-kind-per-address design.
